evidence.target_passage: Short title This Act may be cited as the Not A Trusted Organization Act or the NATO Act . Findings Congress makes the following findings: The North Atlantic Treaty (also known as the Washington Treaty ) was signed on April 4, 1949, in Washington, DC, and created the North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO). NATO was intended to counterbalance the political and military power of the Soviet Union in Eastern Europe and was originally composed of 12 member states representing Western Europe and its transatlantic partners. The preamble to the Washington Treaty affirms that the Parties will unite their efforts for collective defense . Similarly, Article 3 of the Washington Treaty provides that each Party will maintain and develop their individual and collective capacity
